Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Financial Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review Apex Financial Group's results for the third quarter. With me this morning are Mark Reilly, Chief Executive Officer; Jane Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; David Chen, Chief Risk Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Credit Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Operating Officer; Tom Harris, Chief Marketing Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Mark Reilly.

Mark Reilly:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Financial Group delivered record results in the third quarter, exceeding all previous benchmarks and solidifying our position as a leader in the financial services industry.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Sustaining strong revenue growth
2. Driving operational efficiency
3. Managing risk effectively
4. Investing in technology and innovation
5. Enhancing customer experience
6. Strengthening our brand reputation
7. Promoting a diverse and inclusive culture
8. Delivering superior returns to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on key areas of performance. Fee income across wealth management, investment banking, and cards showed robust growth driven by market tailwinds and strategic initiatives. The macroeconomic environment remains resilient with regional variations impacting our portfolios positively overall. We're optimistic on loan growth while maintaining top-tier credit quality. Our efficiency ratio continues to improve toward ambitious targets. Reserves saw a beneficial release supported by strong coverage levels. Risk-weighted assets are under tight control through optimization efforts. Capital ratios, including CET1 and Tier 1, exceed requirements with room for returns. And our asset sensitivity position is managed prudently to handle interest rate dynamics.

I will now turn the call over to Jane Thompson to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jane Thompson:
Thank you, Mark, and good morning. Apex Financial Group reported net income of $2.5 billion for the third quarter, or $1.85 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 12% to $5.2 billion, driven by growth in our loan portfolio and improved net interest margin. Non-interest income was up 14% year-over-year to $2.8 billion, reflecting strong performance in our investment banking and wealth management businesses, alongside cards momentum. We are generating strong returns on equity and are committed to delivering value to our shareholders.

Let me now turn to our fee income performance, which continues to be a cornerstone of our diversified revenue model. In Q3, total non-interest income reached $2.8 billion, up 14% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter, with fee income specifically—excluding trading gains—growing 12% year-over-year to $1.95 billion. This resilience underscores our focus on high-margin, recurring streams amid moderating interest rates and a bifurcated equity market.

Breaking this down by our key pillars: wealth management, investment banking, and cards, representing 42%, 31%, and 27% of total fee income, respectively. Wealth management delivered standout results with advisory and asset management fees at $815 million, up 16% year-over-year. This was powered by assets under management growth to $1.7 trillion, a 12% increase, with market appreciation adding about 7 percentage points from the S&P 500's 8% quarterly rally, especially in tech where our active equity strategies beat benchmarks by 150 basis points. Net new money hit $28 billion, surpassing full-year guidance, driven by high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients. Recurring advisory fees, 65% of segment revenue, saw higher average rates of 52 basis points due to shifts into our Apex Prime alternatives suite, including private credit and infrastructure with $12 billion inflows. North America led with 55% of net new money via our RIA custody platform serving over 1,200 advisors and $450 billion in assets. EMEA grew 22% on sustainable products amid EU SFDR rules, while APAC's 9% rise offset China real estate issues through Singapore family office growth at 35%. Our gen AI-powered Wealth Insights platform, now with 40% advisor adoption, lifted cross-sell by 20% and wallet share by 8%. We anticipate 10-12% fee growth for full-year 2024, targeting $110 billion in net new money via expansions like our India JV with HDFC Asset Management.

Investment banking fees climbed 9% to $605 million, maintaining our #4 global M&A advisory ranking and #3 in ECM per Dealogic. M&A, 48% of fees, rose 12% to $290 million on 15% quarter-over-quarter cross-border uptick in healthcare and tech, including the $15 billion Eli Lilly spin-off and $10 billion European pharma deal. ECM added $180 million, up 5%, from 22 IPOs and follow-ons raising $45 billion, despite Fed cut volatility. DCM grew 14% to $135 million on high-yield and 8% leveraged loan share. A $120 billion advisory backlog, up 20% quarter-over-quarter, signals Q4 strength, with Americas at 60%, EMEA 25% in UK buyouts, and APAC 15% in Australian mining. Our IBX Digital automation cut execution times 30%, boosting mandates 15%, while sponsor coverage taps $2.5 trillion private equity dry powder. We expect 8-10% full-year growth, with upside from rate cuts unlocking U.S. activity.

Cards and payments fees surged 19% to $530 million, exceeding historical CAGR, on 14% purchase volume growth to $285 billion and 11% active accounts to 42 million. Interchange, 62% at $328 million, rode travel and discretionary spend up 22% and 16%, supported by U.S. wage resilience. Apex Black Reserve grew 25% with $45 million fees at 85% rewards redemption. Co-branded partnerships like Visa Signature with Delta added $65 million, up 30%. U.S. led 70% growth on seasonal spending, EMEA 24% via fintech white-labeling like Revolut, APAC 15% despite FX. Tokenization on 80% cards cut fraud 40%, Apple/Google Pay at 65%, and embedded APIs with 500 merchants lifted margins 50 bps. Delinquencies at 2.8% beat FDIC industry 3.2%. We project 16-18% full-year growth, aiming for 5 million premium accounts via app rewards.

Across pillars, 65% recurring fees shield NIM compression, with 28% ROE average. We're deploying $500 million in cloud data lakes and blockchain custody to raise cross-segment share 15%, mirroring JPMorgan's model despite APAC geopolitical and consumer risks. We reaffirm full-year fee income of $7.8-8.0 billion, up 13% midpoint.

Before diving deeper into segments, some color on the macroeconomic backdrop shaping our performance. We've navigated a resilient environment with disinflation, bifurcated growth, and central banks aiming for soft landings. In the U.S., 55% of core banking revenue, GDP grew 2.8% annualized, unemployment at 4.1%, wage growth cooling to 3.9%, core PCE at 2.5%. Consumer spending holds with retail up 0.4% monthly, but credit card utilization at 45% warrants watch on our 1.2% consumer delinquencies. Fed funds steady at 5.25-5.50%, markets eye 75 bps cuts to 3.75-4.00% terminal. Loan book up 5.2% to $450 billion on CRE refinancings (exposure down to 12%) and 7% C&I. Deposit betas at 65% compressed NIM 8 bps to 3.42%; expect 10-15 more bps, but full-year NII $8.2-8.4 billion via $120 billion securities at 4.8% yields.

Europe, 25% international, saw flat GDP at 0.1%, Germany output down 2.5%. ECB cut to 3.50% aids, but services inflation 4.1%. Loans grew 2.1%, NPLs 1.8% below average; IB fees up 15% on €5 billion M&A. APAC, 15%, China at 4.6% GDP hit by property, but ASEAN strong; deposits up $15 billion, loans 3.8%, real estate capped at 8%. Equities volatile with S&P +18% YTD, VIX 22; Markets captured $250 million trading, $30 trillion derivatives hedging geopolitical risks.

Impacts show pristine credit: NPLs 0.85%, provisions 25 bps, $4.2 billion reserve. Consumer auto delinquencies up 20 bps to 1.5%, countered by AI scoring cutting defaults 15%. LCR 145%, NSFR 112%; $2 billion buyback, dividend up 8% to $0.62. Tech transformation with gen-AI risk platform on Palantir Foundry covers 80% loans, cloud cuts IT 12%, $50 billion ESG lending. Base case 2025 global growth 3.1%, U.S. rates 4.25%; mid-single loan growth, NII stable H1, fee expansion on 20% M&A volumes. CET1 12.8%, 60% non-NII revenue resilient.

Turning to loan growth and credit quality outlook, a strategy cornerstone. Full-year 2024 average loans grow 5-6%, from 3.8% in 2023, assuming 2.2% GDP, 4.1% unemployment. Pipeline $12.5 billion, up 15%. C&I leads 7-8%, strong Southeast manufacturing/nearshoring; $2.1 billion YTD at SOFR+285 bps, 2.8 products cross-sell, $800 million SBA. CRE 3-4% in multifamily/industrial; office 8%, Florida/Texas 60% pipeline, cap rates 5.8%, criticized 4.2% below peers. Consumer 4%, auto 6% FICO 740, digital HELOC 25% apps. Deposits up 4.2% to $185 billion, 32% non-interest, NIM to 3.55%.

Credit stable: delinquencies 0.82% vs. FDIC 0.95%, peak 1.0%; NCOs 0.24%, guide 0.25-0.30%; NPLs 0.65%, CECL $2.4 billion or 1.45%, 285% criticized coverage. Moody's ML models improve warnings 18%, DFAST CET1 11.2%. Sunbelt <0.6%, Texas energy stress-tested. Diversify CRE to 20%, $1 billion ABL with fintechs. ROCE to 11.5%.

On efficiency ratio, non-interest expenses over total revenue. Full-year so far improved 320 bps to 57.2% from 60.4%, Q3 at 56.1% best ever, adjusted 55.9%. Matches JPM 56%, beats KBW 61%. Retail 59.4% from 63.1% via 145 branch optimizations, Walmart digital deposits 28% low-cost. Commercial 52.8% from 57.2%, RPA cuts 40% times, 12% pipeline. Wealth 54.3%, robo $450 billion AUM. U.S. 56.5% digital 72%, Europe 60.2% compliance offset UK IBOR, APAC 55.1% API super-apps 35% remittances.

Expenses up 4.2% to $8.7 billion vs. 9.1% revenue. Zero-based budgeting, comp 28.4%. $450 million UniCore NextGen cloud/Temenos, AI fraud $120 million saved, chatbots 30% deflection. Target 54% 2024, sub-52% 2026 for 10-12% EPS. Initiatives: ML personalization 15% cross-sell, virtual branches Meta AR/VR 1,800 sites, RPA reporting $50 million save. Risks inflation/geopolitics, but 55% non-interest, CET1 12.8%.

Regarding provision for credit losses under CECL across $850 billion loans, Q3 $450 million release vs. $1.1 billion build last year, +15 bps ROTCE. NCOs 45 bps down 10 bps, below 55 bps cycle. Delinquencies 1.1%. AI Sentinel flags 20% more pre-delinquency. Macro: GDP 2.4%, unemployment 4.3%, PCE 2.8%; PDs down 15%. U.S. $350 million release mortgages/ cards, Europe $50 million CIB offset CRE overlay, APAC flat China build, RoW neutral. De-risked $15 billion, IFRS 9 hybrid.

ACL $15.2 billion, 1.78% loans up 5 bps QoQ, 3.2x NCOs; NPLs 1.05% 172% coverage vs. JPM 155%; criticized 245% vs. 220% peers; CRE 2.45%. Guide flat-$300 million H2 builds, $2 billion buffer. ROCE 11-12% 2025.

On risk-weighted assets, key to capital. Q3 $1.42 trillion, +2.1% YoY 0.8% QoQ FX-neutral, below peers 4-5%. Intensity 48% from 51%. Credit 82% $1.16 trillion: wholesale 45% 62% RW, retail 37% $430 billion. Market 13% $185 billion SA-CCR +15 bps mitigated. Op risk $75 billion flat SMA.

Trends: CRE migration -25 bps, sold $4.5 billion office $2.8 billion RWA relief. FX +$18 billion. U.S. 65% $920 billion ABS relief, EMEA stable NPLs down, APAC +5% CDS hedged. IRB models 7% reduction $80 billion save, ML PD/LGD, synthetic sec $20 billion $11 billion relief, EIRB divest. IFRS 9 Stage 2/3 4.2%. Buyback $500 million CET1 to 13.2%. Guide $1.40-1.45 trillion 2024, Basel IV 7% impact.

Wrapping financials, our asset sensitivity: modestly asset-sensitive +2.8% NII beta +100 bps. +200 bps +6.8% $285 million, -100 bps -5.0% -$210 million. 92% LDR, 68% floating loans SOFR/Prime, deposits beta 32% 62% sticky. EVE +4.2% +100 bps, asset dur 3.8 vs. liab 3.2. Scenarios: +200 bps +3.1% $1,250 million, -200 -7.8% -$3,150; steepener +1.2%, flattener -4.5%. MSR hedge 105 bps.

U.S. +3.5% C&I/CRE, Europe +0.8% swaps, APAC -1.2% offset India. $65 billion swaps YTD, AOCI -$420 million. ALM Pro AI Palantir/Moody's 70% faster, ML betas. De-risk: CD repricing, brokered 8-12%, adjustable CDs $8 billion, securities to MBS/CLOs. NII -2.1% in -150 bps vs. peers -4.5%. CET1 11.8%, LCR 125%, ROTE >14%.

David Chen:
Thank you, Jane. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring credit migration in commercial real estate, interest rate volatility, geopolitical tensions, and operational cyber threats. We are implementing enhanced controls, including advanced AI monitoring and stress testing, to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile.

Lisa Patel:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains excellent with non-performing loans at 0.65% and delinquencies at 0.82%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio through selective originations and proactive workouts, remaining confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment.

Raj Singh:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are leveraging technology to enhance customer experience, improve efficiency, and drive innovation. Our investments in generative AI platforms like Wealth Insights and ALM Pro, cloud migrations to AWS, and RPA workflows are yielding significant results, including fraud reductions, faster processing, and better decision-making.

Maria Gonzalez:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include streamlining our processes through network optimization, optimizing our infrastructure with zero-based budgeting, and leveraging data analytics to improve decision-making.

Tom Harris:
Thank you. From a marketing perspective, we are focused on strengthening our brand reputation and enhancing customer engagement. Our recent campaigns around premium cards and sustainable products have been highly successful in driving customer acquisition and retention.

Elena Vasquez:
Good morning. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of compliance and ethical conduct. We are continuously strengthening our compliance programs, including DORA preparations and ESG integrations, and working closely with regulators to ensure we are meeting all applicable requirements.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, that is digit 1 to ask a question. Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thanks. Good morning, team. I wanted to dive into your capital position, specifically CET1 and Tier 1 ratios. Could you walk us through the current levels versus regulatory requirements, any trends we're seeing, and how you're thinking about optimization initiatives?

Mark Reilly:
Thanks, Sarah. Happy to unpack our capital ratios—it's a cornerstone of our fortress balance sheet here at Apex Financial Group.

Jane Thompson:
Let me start with the headline numbers from Q3, which reflect another quarter of pristine execution. Our Common Equity Tier 1 ratio—or CET1—stood at 13.8% on a fully loaded Basel III basis as of September 30th, up 40 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 110 basis points year-over-year. That's well above our internal target of 12.5% and comfortably cushions our regulatory minimums. For context, as a G-SIB with a 2.0% surcharge, our Pillar 1 CET1 requirement is 8.0%, plus the capital conservation buffer of 2.5%, countercyclical buffer at 0.5% given current U.S. and EU settings, and our G-SIB bucket, landing us at an all-in CET1 requirement of 10.5% under fully phased-in Basel III rules. We're running a solid 330 basis points above that, which gives us ample dry powder for growth, returns to shareholders, and absorbing any macro tailwinds.

On Tier 1, we're at 15.4%, incorporating our Additional Tier 1 instruments—primarily our €1.5 billion perpetual callable AT1 issuance from last year, which carries a 6.25% fixed-to-floating coupon. That's up 30 bps quarter-over-quarter, driven by strong organic capital generation. Tier 1 requirements mirror CET1 closely but include AT1 eligibility, so our buffer here is even more robust at around 480 bps above the 10.5% all-in floor.

Mark Reilly:
Jane, if I can jump in on the trends—our CET1 trajectory has been textbook. Year-to-date, we've generated 180 bps of capital organically, outpacing our 140-160 bps guidance range, thanks to disciplined expense management and positive operating leverage. Risk-weighted assets grew just 1.2% quarter-over-quarter to $1.07 trillion, moderated by our proactive de-risking in non-core commercial real estate exposures—down 8% in RWAs there amid the office sector headwinds we're all navigating. Compare that to peers like JPMorgan or Wells Fargo, who've seen RWAs expand 3-5% in recent quarters on loan growth; our focus on high-return, low-RWA businesses like wealth management and payments is paying dividends.

Jane Thompson:
Spot on, Mark. Regionally, this plays out differently. In the U.S., where we operate via Apex Bank USA with $450 billion in assets, our CET1 is 14.2%—flawless ahead of the Fed's CCAR stress test next June, where we expect to pass with flying colors under the new large bank rules. We've already prepped for the Basel III Endgame proposals, modeling a 72 bps CET1 impact from expanded credit risk floors and operational risk standardization, but our current position absorbs that fully without curtailing buybacks. In Europe, under ECB supervision, our CET1 at the group level ex-U.S. is 13.5%, exceeding SREP requirements of 10.3% including the 1.5% pillar 2 guidance add-on. We've got ATR 82 status, which keeps management buffer expectations low at 1%. Asia-Pacific, via our Hong Kong and Singapore hubs, clocks in at 14.6% CET1, benefiting from HKMA's conservative countercyclical buffer at zero and our pivot toward digital consumer lending—think our Apex Pay app, which has scaled to 15 million users with RWAs per loan 20% below traditional mortgages.

Strategically, we're laser-focused on RWA efficiency. We've rolled out IFRS 9 stage migration models approved by both Fed and ECB, shifting $20 billion of performing loans from stage 2 to stage 1, releasing 25 bps of CET1. Securitization remains a workhorse: Q3 saw us issue $8 billion in RMBS and auto loan ABS, offloading 2% of credit RWAs at a 15% risk transfer rate—similar to what Citi's been doing successfully. On the tech side, our proprietary AI-driven IRB model recalibration for corporate portfolios shaved another 10 bps, pending final regulatory nod. Looking forward, we're guiding to 13.5-14.0% CET1 by year-end, supporting $4 billion in buybacks and a 55% payout ratio on EPS.

We've also stress-tested against a repeat of 2023's regional banking mini-crisis: under a -25% equity shock and 300 bps rate hike, we still exit at 10.8% CET1—150 bps above requirements. This positions us ideally for M&A, like our pending $2.5 billion acquisition of a Midwest regional wealth platform, which is RWA-accretive at just 0.8x.

Sarah Jenkins:
That's comprehensive—thanks, team.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez:
What is your outlook for deposit growth and funding costs in a rate-cutting environment?

Jane Thompson:
Good morning, Mike. Our outlook remains constructive, with deposits projected to grow 4-5% full-year, supported by our sticky core at 62% low-beta and initiatives like adjustable-rate CDs and embedded finance partnerships. Funding costs should stabilize as betas moderate further to 30%, preserving NIM around 3.45% even with 75 bps Fed cuts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Can you discuss the impact of regulatory changes like Basel III Endgame on your RWA and capital plans?

David Chen:
Thanks, Emily. We've modeled a manageable 72 bps CET1 hit, already absorbed through RWA optimization like IRB enhancements and securitizations. We'll maintain CET1 above 13%, prioritizing organic growth and returns without altering buyback or dividend strategies.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
What are your plans for further technology investments, particularly in AI and cloud?

Raj Singh:
Good morning, David. We're allocating another $500 million in 2025 to expand gen AI across risk, customer service, and personalization, alongside full cloud migration. This builds on successes like 70% faster ALM modeling and 20% cross-sell lifts, targeting 15% efficiency gains.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Mark Reilly for any closing remarks.

Mark Reilly:
Thank you for your interest in Apex Financial Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
